name: Ansible
tagline: Agentless, idempotent automation: bring servers to a known state over SSH.

howItWorks.title: Control node and inventory
howItWorks.body:
The control node holds playbooks, roles and inventory.
Inventory groups hosts; group_vars override per group.
Targets need only SSH and Python.
Forks run tasks on hosts in parallel.

howItWorks.title: Modules and idempotency
howItWorks.body:
Each task calls a module such as apt, user or lineinfile.
Modules compare desired and actual state.
The recap reports ok, changed or failed per host.
command and shell always report changed unless guarded.

howItWorks.title: Roles, handlers and templates
howItWorks.body:
Roles package tasks, handlers, templates and defaults.
Handlers run once at the end, only when notified.
Jinja2 templates render per-host files.
validate: tests a file before it replaces the original.

howItWorks.title: Check mode and diff
howItWorks.body:
--check simulates the run and changes nothing.
--diff prints the exact file changes.
--limit scopes the run to one host or group.
A second run with changed=0 proves idempotency.

howItWorks.title: On-prem bring-up
howItWorks.body:
Create users, keys and sudoers drop-ins first.
Harden sshd: no passwords, no root, AllowUsers.
Set chrony, firewall rules and cron jobs.
Cron or CI re-runs the baseline to correct drift.

flow: Control node reads inventory and selects the hosts.
It opens SSH sessions in parallel, default five forks.
Modules are copied to each host and executed.
Each module compares desired state with actual state.
Changed tasks notify handlers, such as an sshd restart.
Handlers run once at the end of the play.
The recap reports ok, changed, unreachable and failed.

deploy.summary: Bring up on-prem hosts: control node, inventory, then a baseline role with SSH hardening, chrony, firewall and cron.
prerequisites: Target Ubuntu hosts with SSH and a sudo user
Static IPs and DNS for each host
A console or second SSH session as fallback

steps.title: Control node and SSH key
steps.code:
python3 -m venv ~/ansible-venv && . ~/ansible-venv/bin/activate
pip install 'ansible-core==2.18.6'
ansible-galaxy collection install ansible.posix:1.6.2 community.general:10.7.0
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_ops -C ops@control
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_ops.pub ops@10.0.10.11
steps.note: Repeat ssh-copy-id per host. Needs Python 3.11+ on the control node.

steps.title: Inventory, config and connectivity
steps.code:
mkdir -p ~/infra/{inventory,roles} && cd ~/infra
cat > ansible.cfg <<'EOF'
[defaults]
inventory = inventory/hosts.ini
private_key_file = ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_ops
host_key_checking = True
[privilege_escalation]
become = True
EOF
cat > inventory/hosts.ini <<'EOF'
[web]
web01 ansible_host=10.0.10.11
web02 ansible_host=10.0.10.12
[db]
db01 ansible_host=10.0.10.21
[all:vars]
ansible_user=ops
EOF
ansible all -m ansible.builtin.ping
steps.note: Replace the addresses with your hosts. Expect SUCCESS and pong from each.

steps.title: Ad-hoc commands
steps.code:
ansible all -a 'uptime'
ansible web -m ansible.builtin.setup -a 'filter=ansible_distribution*'
ansible web -b -m ansible.builtin.apt -a 'name=chrony state=present update_cache=yes'
ansible db -b -m ansible.builtin.service -a 'name=cron state=started enabled=true'
ansible all -b -m ansible.builtin.shell -a 'df -h /' --limit web01
steps.note: Ad-hoc is for one-off checks. Anything repeatable belongs in a role.

steps.title: Users and sudoers role
steps.code:
# roles/baseline/tasks/users.yml
- name: Create admin user
  ansible.builtin.user: { name: deploy, groups: sudo, shell: /bin/bash, append: true }
- name: Install authorized key
  ansible.posix.authorized_key: { user: deploy, key: "{{ lookup('file', '~/.ssh/id_ed25519_ops.pub') }}" }
- name: Passwordless sudo for deploy
  ansible.builtin.copy:
    dest: /etc/sudoers.d/deploy
    content: "deploy ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL\n"
    mode: '0440'
    validate: /usr/sbin/visudo -cf %s
steps.note: visudo validation stops a bad sudoers file from locking you out.

steps.title: SSH hardening with validation
steps.note: Keep a second session open. The service is ssh on Debian and sshd on RHEL.

steps.title: Chrony, firewall and cron
steps.note: Always add the SSH allow rule before enabling the firewall.

steps.title: Check, diff, apply, prove idempotency
steps.code:
cat > site.yml <<'EOF'
- hosts: all
  roles: [baseline]
EOF
ansible-playbook site.yml --syntax-check
ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff --limit web01
ansible-playbook site.yml
ansible-playbook site.yml   # second run must show changed=0
steps.note: Check mode predicts changes; diff shows the exact lines. Roll out to one host first.

verify: ansible all -m ping returns SUCCESS and pong for every host.
Second ansible-playbook run ends with changed=0 and failed=0.
ssh root@web01 is denied; sshd -t exits 0.
chronyc tracking shows a reference ID and small offset.
pitfalls: Enabling ufw before allowing port 22 locks you out.
shell and command report changed unless creates: or changed_when: is set.
Ubuntu sshd_config.d drop-ins can override your sshd_config lines.
Missing AllowUsers entry for your own user blocks your own login.
Skip validate: on sshd_config and a typo kills SSH.
Unpinned collections change behaviour between runs.
keyPoints: Agentless: the control node pushes modules over SSH.
Idempotent tasks converge state and report changed only on drift.
Inventory, roles and handlers make bring-up repeatable.
Run --check --diff first; keep secrets in Ansible Vault.
quickDeploy: Install pinned ansible-core and an SSH key
Write inventory and test with ping
Apply a baseline role: users, SSH, chrony, firewall
osiNote: Application-layer automation over SSH on TCP 22.
production: Pin ansible-core and collection versions in a requirements file.
Run playbooks from CI with --check --diff as a gate.
Roll out with --limit and serial: one host, then batches.
Vault-encrypt secrets; keep the key out of the repository.
Log runs and alert on failed or unreachable hosts.
